headline: 2013 executive order keeps a set of existing federal advisory committees running instead of letting them expire.
what_it_does: This order extends the life of certain federal advisory committees, which are groups that give advice to the President and federal agencies. Without an extension, many such committees end automatically after a set time. Orders like this are usually issued every two years, but the title alone does not name which committees are covered or exactly how long they continue.

who_it_affects.how: Their committees can keep meeting and giving advice instead of shutting down.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that rely on these committees
who_it_affects.how: They keep getting outside advice from the committees covered by the order.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 30, 2013; the end date of the extension is not given in the title.
